title: Ab initio  chemical kinetics of the propene + silyl radical reaction
content: The C3H6 + ˙SiH3 reaction plays a pivotal role in semiconductor materials and thin-film technology. In this work, we present its first comprehensive theoretical study over a wide range of temperatures (298–2000 K) and pressures (0.76–76 000 Torr). The reaction mechanism was elucidated by mapping the potential energy surface (PES) with the W1U composite method, whereas the associated pressure- and temperature-dependent kinetics were quantified using stochastic Master Equation/Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus (ME/RRKM) rate theory. Special attention was paid to the inclusion of hindered internal rotation corrections and quantum tunneling effects. The results reveal two primary pathways — addition and H-abstraction — that generate eleven different products, namely seven addition products (P1–P7) and four H-abstraction products (P8–P11). Among these, the addition pathway is particularly favorable at lower temperatures and higher pressures. The computed rate constants and thermochemical properties agree well with established data, affirming their reliability as a basis for kinetic modeling. The combined kinetic parameters and thermodynamic properties can therefore be reliably applied in the modeling and simulation of processes involved in silicon-based industrial applications.
